Subject: New procurement: throughput profile and short microburst tolerance

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the intro earlier. We're at the stage where procurement needs a clear picture of what Dedicated capacity we'd need to meet our SLA. A few specifics from our side:

- Typical steady-state: ~45k tokens/sec across our inference fleet (mixed request sizes, avg 80 tokens/req).
- Expected peak microbursts: up to 110k tokens/sec for short windows (~8-20s) when a campaign triggers.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 180ms for the primary endpoint; 99th under 300ms preferred.
- We plan a phased roll: pilot (Q2) -> ramp (Q3) -> full (Q4).

Can your team give a recommended Dedicated capacity runway (baseline GPUs + burst cushion) and note any tradeoffs (batching, quantization impact, cache hit assumptions)? We've attached a high-level ML profile and our SLA doc.

Appreciate the detail,
Alex

Subject: Venturis capacity runway: first-pass numbers and assumptions

Alex / team — attached is our first-pass capacity model (capacity_model_v1.xlsx). High level summary below; I'll follow up with a quick walk-through.

Assumptions we used (please confirm):
- Model family: open-llm-v2-m (approx 70B dense equivalent); typical per-GPU sustained throughput = 3,800 tokens/sec for 4k context in our benchmarked config.
- KV / prefix caching: expected hit rate 18% during campaigns, 45% during steady-state (we used 30% blended).
- Average request token length: 80 tokens; average response tokens: 60 tokens (total 140 tokens per call).
- Microburst shape: triangular spike to peak over 4s, sustain 12s, decay 4s (total ~20s) — matched Alex's window.

Recommended fleet sizing (numeric):
- Steady-state (45k tokens/sec): ~12 GPUs (45,000 / 3,800 ≈ 11.8)
- Peak microburst (110k tokens/sec): ~29 GPUs raw (110,000 / 3,800 ≈ 28.9)
- Practical proposal: baseline reserve 13 GPUs (round up + 5% ops cushion) + burst pool of 18 GPUs available for autoscale—total committed footprint 31 GPUs, with 18 as preemptible/burstable to reduce cost.

Latency SLO fit notes: with this split and conservative batching (~25ms batching window) we expect 95p latency ≈ 140–170ms in the steady-state. During full microburst with autoscale cold starts, 95p could spike above 300ms unless we keep a small hot buffer (we modeled 4 GPUs hot beyond baseline to absorb immediate burst ingress).

Tradeoffs / suggestions:
- Quantization to int4 can improve per-GPU throughput by ~1.6x; if you can tolerate a small accuracy delta, baseline GPUs could be reduced accordingly.
- Larger batching reduces token cost but increases tail latency; we recommend a dynamic batching policy keyed off route priority.
- Suggest a canary with 4 GPUs and a synthetic microburst to validate autoscale ramp timing.

[Attachment: capacity_model_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Happy to run alternative scenarios if you can confirm model family / desired accuracy targets.

Quick technical addendum from the runtime side — calling out microburst sensitivity and mitigation levers.

Key points:
1) Cold-start / scaling latency: our Dedicated autoscaler can provision GPUs in ~45–90s depending on region and quota; that is too slow for an 8–20s spike. To meet their SLO during those bursts we need a hot buffer (N_hot). In Ben's model above, N_hot ≈ 4 GPUs is realistic to cap 95p spikes.
2) KV cache effect: with a 30% blended hit-rate we get an effective tokens/sec reduction for the host pool. If Venturis can push more requests with stable prefixes (higher cacheability), steady-state GPUs drop noticeably.
3) Batching window sensitivity: we modeled 0ms/10ms/25ms. 25ms gave best cost, 10ms gave balanced latency/cost, and 0ms best latency but worse cost. For the 95p <= 180ms target, a 10–15ms window + N_hot=4 keeps most scenarios inside SLO during microbursts.
4) Canary / fallback plan: run a canary with an engineered microburst at 1.2x expected peak to measure tail. Implement automatic fallback to a smaller but faster quantized variant if end-to-end latency surpasses 250ms for >30s.

Open question for Venturis: are you comfortable with a mixed model approach (dense for high-quality queries, quantized for lower-priority routes)? If so, we can size two pools and route by priority to reduce committed footprint.

—Priyom
